_comment: Self-contained ADO daemon profile for the Astra repo. Select with `CodeReviewDaemon --review astra`. Repo coordinates come from Revobot's repos.json entry named 'Astra' (orgUrl o365exchange, project Weve_DA, repository Astra, localPath Q:/repos/Astra) — that entry carries no excludedAuthors, so nothing is filtered here. Modeled on appsettings.mcqdb.json: same two-model split (dispatcher/state orchestrator on ReviewModelId gpt-5.6-luna, code-reviewer:* sub-agents on SubAgentModelId gpt-5.6-sol, sent to the review host at conversation provision and applied to every spawn that does not name its own model or tier; until that channel existed SubAgentModelId had no reader and every sub-agent ran the orchestrator's model, and it takes effect only on a review host running this build or newer, from that host's next restart). Comment posting is OFF — per ADO-ONBOARDING.md a freshly-onboarded repo is collect-only until you explicitly flip EnableCommentPosting. NOTE: the absolute paths below are machine-specific and were written for THIS box (WSL; repo at /home/gautamb/sources/repos/LmDotnetTools, only C: and Q: exist on the Windows side — there is no B: drive, so the B:/... paths in the achieveai/mcqdb/s2s profiles are from a different machine and were deliberately NOT copied). See ADO-ONBOARDING.md.

Ado._comment: azure-devops-mcp public client id (see LmStreaming.Sample/AuthProviderGuide.md). MSAL.NET interactive (browser + loopback + PKCE), no secret. TenantId is pinned to the Microsoft corp tenant rather than 'common' (which mcqdb uses): o365exchange is backed by that tenant — a token issued from it was verified against this repo — and pinning stops MSAL from offering a personal MSA that can never see Astra. Sign in ONCE out-of-band into the shared TokenStoreDir below; the daemon has no `auth` subcommand and restores the sign-in at boot via OAuthTokenHydrator.

SandboxGateway._comment: WorkspaceBasePath is deliberately NOT set here. The daemon does need one (UseS2SReviewAgent makes it mandatory: Program.cs throws 'no workspace base path is configured' because S2SReviewWorkspacePreparer clones the PR checkout host-side into {base}/{leaf} and the gateway mounts that same directory), but it is a property of the RUNNING GATEWAY, not of this profile — and the gateway exposes no way to read it back. Probed 2026-08-06: api/v1/config, api/v1/info and api/v1/workspaces all 404; the only endpoints are /health, api/v1/sandboxes and api/v1/marketplaces/preview. So the client SDK cannot discover it and this profile must not hardcode it. Supply it at launch through CRD_WORKSPACE_BASE_PATH (Program.cs prefers that env var over this key), read from the gateway rather than copied by hand — see ADO-ONBOARDING.md for the launch line. The 'shared host, shared gateway' topology that S2S assumes was verified on this box: a file written from WSL appears inside the gateway container at the identical path. AUTH_ENFORCE=false on this gateway, so CRD_SANDBOX_APP_KEY is not needed.

CodeReviewDaemon._LmStreamingReviewMarketplace_comment: VERIFIED 2026-08-06 against this box's gateway: the alias is 'gb', not the 'gb-plugins' the achieveai/mcqdb/s2s profiles use (those were written for a different gateway). GET api/v1/marketplaces/preview?marketplaces=gb-plugins returns 400 'unknown marketplace alias(es)' with available=[local,superpowers,gb], which with RequireSkillSupport=true would stop the daemon at boot. 'gb' carries code-reviewer 1.19.0 (pr-review skill + 13 code-reviewer:* agents), so the fail-fast check passes.
CodeReviewDaemon._EnableCommentPosting_comment: Collect-only. Astra has active PRs today, so flipping this to true immediately posts Revobot threads to a live, shared repo — leave it false until a collect-only run has been eyeballed in astra-review.db.
CodeReviewDaemon._EnabledRepos_comment: ADO entries are 'org/project/repo' (3 segments) — PrPollTargetBuilder reads them positionally as OrgOrOwner/Project/RepoName. repos.json gives the legacy orgUrl form https://o365exchange.visualstudio.com/; the org segment here is the dev.azure.com equivalent, per the ADO-ONBOARDING warning against *.visualstudio.com. Astra's default branch is main, so PRs are reviewed against base main.
CodeReviewDaemon._ReviewedRepoSubmodules_comment: Intentionally absent: the Astra checkout has no .gitmodules, so there are no first-party nested submodules to allow-list. Add the URL repo-name segments here if that changes — the list is an explicit allow-list, never a same-org wildcard.
CodeReviewDaemon._store_comment: RESOLVED 2026-08-06: the store is github.com/gautamb_microsoft/NOVA_reviews, which carries repos/Astra as a submodule alongside four siblings. The AstraReview repo this profile previously named was never created — a listing of Weve_DA (35 repos) contains no review store — so every run failed at ContextReady with TF401019. NOTE the store is a GitHub superproject whose submodules are ADO repos: the store clone authenticates with github.json, each submodule fetch with the ADO token. repos/Astra is declared with the legacy https://o365exchange.visualstudio.com/Weve_DA/_git/Astra URL, which SubmoduleTargetsRepo now canonicalizes before pairing, so this profile does pair with the store. It still reviews only Astra and co-locates no siblings — prefer appsettings.nova.json, which covers all five repos in this store and grants cross-repo context.
CodeReviewDaemon._ReviewPoolHostRoot_comment: Deliberately unset — it would be inert here, and setting it would only look like it mattered. Program.cs derives poolLeaf from ReviewPoolHostRoot's final segment, but the S2S branch immediately overrides poolRoot to effectiveWorkspaceBase and switches the slot prefix to 'review-slot-', discarding that leaf. With UseS2SReviewAgent=true the pool therefore always lands directly under the gateway-supplied base, which is another reason this profile carries no absolute workspace path.
CodeReviewDaemon._KnowledgeModelId_comment: SPEND-NEUTRALITY PIN. This key was inert on the S2S path until S2SReviewAgentLoopFactory started forwarding modelId as the conversation's provider id; its previous value here was 'claude-opus-4.8', which the factory silently ignored, so the at-close extraction passes have in fact been running on gpt-5.6-luna. Pinned to the model actually in use so the plumbing fix changes no spend. Restoring 'claude-opus-4.8' is now a real, one-token config edit — and it will now take effect.
